answer: Identity rent escalation. Each new identity pays a periodic fee that rises with the count already tied to the same operator, verified through payout graph clustering, so a sybil sweep creates a detectable ripple across shared funding paths. The operator, not the wallet, absorbs the cost: every additional identity multiplies the rent until expansion is unprofitable. This keeps honest users on a flat mesa of predictable fees while attackers climb a steepening slope, and the fee pool funds a garden of legitimate services to offset compliance overhead.
